terms.definition: The scope of actions an agent is permitted to take without human approval — including which tools, data, and downstream agents it may invoke. Agency boundaries determine where policy enforcement and failure attribution apply.
terms.scopeNote: Expanding agency increases accuracy and reliability risk surface. Evaluation must state the agency envelope in force for a scenario.
terms.literatureNote: Used in agent governance literature; AAIF links agency to attribution — errors may be policy/configuration failures rather than model reasoning failures.

terms.definition: The functional parts that make up an agent: the model, system prompt, skills, context assembly, tools, memory, planners, and verification steps. Failures may be attributed to a specific component when observability supports it.
terms.scopeNote: Supports component-level diagnosis without collapsing the agent into model-only evaluation.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.

terms.definition: The objective the agent is instructed to pursue for a task, which should align with user intent but can diverge through misconfiguration, drift, or hijacking.
terms.scopeNote: Goal misalignment is a reasoning failure distinct from a wrong fact in an otherwise aligned task. With user intent, defines WHAT the agent should pursue.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.

terms.definition: The versioned description of an agent under test: model choice, system prompt, skills, tool bindings, memory settings, and policy hooks. Metrics are only comparable across runs that share the same specification version.
terms.scopeNote: Charter assumption: reproducible evaluation requires versioned agent specifications.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.

terms.definition: The shared objective the multi-agent system is configured to pursue — which may differ from any single agent's local goal or from the end user's intent if coordination or delegation is misconfigured.
terms.scopeNote: Coordination failures and cross-agent factual misalignment are measured against multi-agent intent and final system output, not only per-agent goals.
terms.literatureNote: Implicit in MAS benchmarks; AAIF names it so evaluation envelopes can declare what 'success' means at the system boundary.

terms.definition: The ordered set of steps an agent intends to take to reach a goal, including tool use, delegation, and checkpoints. Evaluated for coherence with the goal and feasibility with available tools and permissions.
terms.scopeNote: Planning errors can cause task failure even when individual steps execute correctly.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.

terms.definition: An optional extension to the evaluation subject that includes infrastructure delivery, world or authoritative sources, or user and operator behaviour in what is measured and attributed — without changing the named object (agent, MAS, or workflow).
terms.scopeNote: Rings: infrastructure (platform, cost, availability), world (grounding, trust anchors), user (context, re-prompt, HITL). Declared in the evaluation envelope.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.

terms.definition: A packaged unit of instructions, tools, and optional resources that extends what an agent can do — loaded selectively for a task rather than baked into the base system prompt alone.
terms.scopeNote: Skill selection errors are agent-side configuration or planning failures. Skill versions belong in the agent specification for attribution and reproducibility. Skill adherence measures HOW well a loaded skill was followed.
terms.literatureNote: Emerging in agent frameworks as modular capability bundles. AAIF treats skills as specification artefacts needed for error attribution, not as a separate quality dimension.

terms.definition: The fixed or versioned instruction text that defines an agent's role, constraints, and default behaviour before user messages and retrieved context are assembled. Part of the agent specification and a primary input to context assembly.
terms.scopeNote: Changes to the system prompt are configuration changes — not user intent. Must be pinned for reproducible evaluation and traceability when attributing reasoning failures.
terms.literatureNote: Universal in tool-using agent deployments; rarely named separately in benchmarks but required for audit and specification validation.

terms.definition: The sequence of reasoning steps, tool calls, messages, and state changes an agent or system follows while handling a task. Used to evaluate process accuracy, trajectory consistency, skill adherence, and failure attribution.
terms.scopeNote: In WHAT/HOW framing, trajectory is the primary HOW artefact — the path taken — distinct from intent (WHAT). ARWG defines what trajectory evidence is needed for evaluation; trace emission formats belong to Observability WG.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.

terms.definition: What the user wanted accomplished, including constraints and success criteria, which may differ from the literal wording of a prompt. Accuracy and task completion claims must state how intent was inferred or annotated.
terms.scopeNote: Central to contextual correctness and user-perceived reliability in the charter. In WHAT/HOW framing, user intent (with agent goal and multi-agent intent) defines WHAT success means; trajectory and process dimensions define HOW work was performed.
terms.literatureNote: Foundational for Generally accepted in agent evaluation; AAIF adds scope-ring and workflow disambiguation.
